detail.abstract: We review research on articial intelligence (AI), platform work and algorithmic management. We ask what measures of AI's eects on work actually measure, and how research on the workers who use AI relates to research on the workers who produce it. To answer both questions, we conduct a structured narrative synthesis of 98 records spanning research on labour-market measurement, the labour process, data work and governance. We code 81 of these records on 23 elds and map the coded corpus as a co-classication network. We nd that impact estimates track their data sources, that the Global North supplies most quantitative evidence on exposure, adoption and impact, and that the two literatures divide even within a corpus we assembled to connect them. Joining the two literatures through the transnational value chain, we recast the future of work as a question of who sets the chain's terms and on what evidence. We draw implications for measurement practice and for Convention No. 193, the new international labour standard on decent work in the platform economy.

detail.abstract: This study addresses the shortage of trucking drivers in Mexico from a qualitative perspective, exploring the working conditions that influence driver attrition and the difficulty in recruiting new workers. Through semi-structured interviews with thirty drivers and twenty-four trip scheduling managers at transportation companies, work-related, personal, and psychosocial factors that explain the phenomenon were identified. The analysis, based on qualitative coding with a grounded theory approach, revealed that, despite competitive incomes, drivers face grueling workdays, safety risks, precarious road conditions, and a lack of social and organizational recognition. Most interviewees reported physical and mental health problems stemming from the work process, including chronic fatigue, stress, sleep disturbances, and substances used to stay alert. Structural barriers to generational renewal were also identified, such as a lack of public policies, formal training, and professional attractiveness for new generations. Companies, for their part, acknowledge the difficulty of retaining talent due to the deteriorating working conditions and the lack of incentives. It concludes that the driver shortage is not explained exclusively by economic factors, but by the accumulation of occupational hazards, organizational demands, and the lack of strategies to professionalize and dignify work. The study suggests the urgent need for multisectoral interventions to improve working conditions, reduce turnover, and promote the sustainability of road transport.

title: Analyzing the Linguistic Markers of Emotional Expression in Older Consumers' Complaints

detail.abstract: Consumer complaints constitute an important mechanism through which consumers seek redress and interact with consumer protection systems. Although previous research has examined whether older consumers complain following unsatisfactory marketplace experiences, considerably less is known about how they communicate their complaints. This study examines age-related differences in the emotional expression of formal written consumer complaints submitted to the Israeli Consumer Protection and Fair Trade Authority. The analysis is based on 2,182 complaints submitted in 2023, including 214 complaints from consumers aged 65+ and 1,968 from consumers aged 18-64. Using HeBERT and HebEMO, a Hebrew-language natural language processing model and emotion-classification tool, complaints were analyzed for sentiment polarity (positive, neutral, or negative) and eight discrete emotions. No significant age-group difference was found in the proportion of complaints classified as negative, providing no support for H1. Across the eight discrete emotions, anger was the only emotion for which a significant age-group difference emerged. Complaints submitted by consumers aged 65+ were less likely to be classified as expressing anger (43.0% vs. 54.6%) and showed a lower mean model-assigned probability of anger presence (M = .438 vs. .546) than complaints submitted by consumers aged 18-64. No significant age-group differences were found for the other seven emotions. These findings suggest that age-related differences in the emotional expression of consumer complaints may be emotion-specific rather than reflecting a general reduction in emotional expression. By shifting attention from whether older consumers complain to how they communicate when they do complain, the study identifies anger expression as a previously understudied dimension of older consumers' engagement with consumer protection systems.

title: Change Data Capture Architectures for Real-Time Data Warehousing: Patterns from Production Oracle GoldenGate Deployments
affiliations: Meghnad Saha Institute of Technology

detail.title: Change Data Capture Architectures for Real-Time Data Warehousing: Patterns from Production Oracle GoldenGate Deployments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No external fund used

detail.abstract: Enterprise data warehouses fed by scheduled batch ETL carry an inherent staleness penalty: data reflects the state of the source system as of the last extraction window, commonly up to 24 hours out of date in traditional nightly-batch designs. Change Data Capture (CDC), particularly log-based CDC that reads directly from a database's redo or transaction log, eliminates this penalty by propagating committed changes to downstream systems continuously rather than periodically. This paper examines CDC architectural patterns through the lens of Oracle GoldenGate, the log-based CDC platform underlying a large share of production real-time data warehousing deployments, and grounds its analysis in officially published Oracle customer case studies and independent CDC benchmark data rather than vendor claims alone. We compare batch ETL, query-based polling CDC, trigger-based CDC, and log-based CDC along latency and sourcesystem-overhead dimensions, finding published figures of 5-30 second latency for polling-based CDC against sub-100-millisecond latency for log-based CDC, with corresponding throughput differences of roughly two orders of magnitude. We examine three officially documented production deployments: a Korean ecommerce retailer that reduced daily batch load time from 9 hours to 2 hours by replacing batch ETL with GoldenGate-fed warehouse loading; a manufacturer that achieved 15x faster results publishing and 50% lower business intelligence infrastructure cost by streaming GoldenGate change data to Kafka and HDFS at a reported 180-200 million transactions per load; and a documented case in which month-end transaction volume exceeding 50 million records caused multi-hour replication lag, illustrating that log-based CDC's latency advantage is not unconditional under extreme source-side load. We synthesize these patterns into a reusable CDC integration architecture spanning trail-file staging design, reconciliation and validation, lag monitoring, and schema evolution handling, along with an evaluation methodology for teams designing CDC-fed real-time warehousing pipelines.

detail.abstract: Rebranding is a relevant strategy for addressing changes in the business environment; however, its success is not determined solely by changes in visual identity. This paper aims to analyze the impact of rebranding on brand equity and product competitiveness and to develop a conceptual framework that integrates marketing strategies with public policy compliance. This study employs a conceptual approach through a synthesis of literature on brand equity, brand repositioning, country-of-origin effect, competitive advantage, as well as intellectual property rights (IPR) and data protection regulations. The discussion shows that rebranding has a dual impact. On the one hand, brand changes can improve efficiency, expand markets, renew brand image, and strengthen corporate control. On the other hand, rebranding can lead to brand equity dilution, consumer resistance, and increased costs of market communication and education. The conceptual framework developed in this paper positions IPR compliance as an enabler, brand asset transfer as a transition mechanism, consumer response as a connecting factor, and competitiveness as the outcome. The success of rebranding depends on achieving a balance between economic efficiency, brand equity continuity, communication, and legal legitimacy.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes a retail sales-promotion mechanism in which, after checkout, each customer selects a number from a category-specific range. At the close of a fixed period, the seller designates the number associated with the lowest aggregate revenue as the "winning" number, and refunds the full purchase price to every customer who selected it. We give a formal description of the mechanism, derive a closedform expression for the seller's expected profit, and show that profit is bounded below by a simple function of the profit margin and the number of available choices, provided customers choose independently of one another. We then identify a structural weakness that the original proposal did not address: because running totals are shown to customers in real time, rational customers have an incentive to migrate toward whichever number currently shows the lowest total, which can undermine the very independence assumption the profit bound relies on. We discuss this and other open issues-regulatory classification, empirical validation, and the mechanism's relationship to existing promotional and prizelinked schemes-that require further work or a business decision by the proponent before the scheme could be considered ready for formal submission or deployment.

detail.abstract: Rebranding through brand renaming is a strategic decision that can reshape brand equity, consumer responses, product competitiveness, and corporate adaptation to institutions. This conceptual study develops a framework examining how brand renaming influences 2 competitiveness in domestic and international markets. The analysis synthesizes Brand Equity Theory, Brand Extension and Brand Architecture, Brand Repositioning Theory, and Consumer Learning Theory, while incorporating public policy, regulation, and intellectual property considerations. The discussion indicates that rebranding can enhance market relevance when the new identity aligns with changing consumer expectations, digital transformation, product development, and evolving value propositions. It may also create opportunities for resource reallocation when firms reduce dependence on licensed brands. Conversely, renaming can disrupt brand recall, create consumer confusion, weaken accumulated brand equity, and generate implementation costs that compete with innovation investment. The study concludes that rebranding outcomes depend on balancing identity transformation with continuity, product value, consumer experience, legal protection, and strategic resource allocation.

detail.abstract: Employee retention plays a crucial role in maintaining workforce stability and organizational continuity, particularly among accounting employees whose functions are essential to financial management and regulatory compliance. This study examined the factors related to retention among accounting employees in a construction company in the Philippines. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were collected from 43 accounting employees through an electronic self-administered questionnaire using a four-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics were used to assess the factors related to retention and the level of employee retention, while Spearman's rank-order correlation was employed to examine their relationships. Results showed that compensation and benefits, career development opportunities, work environment, leadership and supervisory support, job satisfaction, and work-life balance were positively assessed, with leadership and supervisory support receiving the most favorable assessment. Employee retention was also positively assessed. Statistical findings revealed significant positive relationships between all six factors and employee retention, with job satisfaction showing the strongest relationship, followed by work environment. Based on these findings, retention strategies were proposed to sustain favorable workplace conditions and strengthen areas associated with employee retention. The findings support the relevance of Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory and provide management with practical and managerial guidance for developing targeted retention initiatives related to supportive leadership, employee development, job satisfaction, workplace conditions, compensation and benefits, and work-life balance.

detail.abstract: Whether enrolling in graduate school pays has long been a matter of discussion. Using ten annual waves of a large Japanese panel survey that observes people while they are still students, we trace the short-term income path associated with enrollment in a master's program. After the master's program period, the estimated short-term income premium is positive but statistically indistinguishable from zero. The cumulative resource position remains negative throughout the observed early-career period, even before considering tuition. Scenario calculations indicate that recovering this deficit may take substantially longer than the period we observe. These results imply that evaluating graduate education from cross-sectional wage premiums alone can obscure substantial forgone earnings and a potentially long recovery period. Focusing on non-wage amenities, our results show that among those in work, master's entrants report greater flexibility in working hours and location than bachelor's leavers. This descriptive comparison suggests that part of the return to graduate education may be delivered as non-wage benefits rather than as pay.

title: The Body as a Deictic System The Orienting Reflex, Two Reading Programs, and the Special Case of the Nail Plate
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Body as a Deictic System The Orienting Reflex, Two Reading Programs, and the Special Case of the Nail Plate

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial, professional, or personal interests that could have influenced the research or its interpretation.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study is theoretical and conceptual in nature and did not involve human participants, patients, identifiable personal data, or experimental interventions.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: The paper proposes a theoretical model of the body as a deictic system in which the orienting response (Program 0) opens access to two modes of reading: the search for an external referent relative to the origo (Program 1) and the calibration of the addressee's stance toward the signal source itself (Program 2). The focal case is the nail plate, treated as a binary differential feature of hand orientation and as a potential social marker. The strong version of the model requires both programs to operate simultaneously within a single addressed gesture and is therefore formulated as a falsifiable hypothesis rather than an established fact. The model is extended with mechanisms of habituation and dishabituation, supernormal stimulation, contextual modulation, and signal interference. A distinct contribution is the proposal that resources expand not only the intensity of a signal but also the repertoire of its admissible transformations under a preserved invariant; unlike in Veblen and Simmel, the change of form is derived here from the mechanics of repeated capture by Program 0. The boundary of Program 2 is set by addressedness: an involuntarily observed feature may shape an impression, but the deictic hypothesis applies only when the feature is incorporated into an act recognized as addressed. Fourteen testable hypotheses are formulated, including contrastive tests of addressedness and of the strong dual-program status of the nail surface.

title: Everyone Is a Manager: AI Use as an Act of Management
affiliations: Cornell University - Cornell SC Johnson College of Business and Monash University

detail.title: Everyone Is a Manager: AI Use as an Act of Management

detail.abstract: When a knowledge worker is given an AI assistant, they stop executing tasks and start delegating them. Thus, we propose that the use of AI is an act of management, which helps explain the heterogeneity in returns to AI use observed across firms. We model the return to AI as moderated by two managerial abilities: direction (how well the worker specifies what they delegate) and verification (how reliably they catch the tool's errors). As AI becomes more reliable, the skill with the higher marginal return shifts from verification to direction. To the extent that use builds skill, workers develop their managerial abilities in the normal course of work, but as the tool improves, direction will continue to build while verification will not. As increasingly fewer tasks are worth checking, the skill collapses. Workers will reach that point sooner if they only bear part of the cost of their errors. In equilibrium, the strongest verifiers tend to sort into the jobs where collapse is most costly.

detail.abstract:
The article treats demand for a branded product as an exchange order book. Market capacity is limited, and every car sold takes a part of it: a car bought from one brand will not be bought from another. Market share is counted in money, not in units. The model is calculated for three brands with one price, in one segment and with an identical car; the marks differ only in the trust of those around them. Capacity is divided in proportion to trust: with trust of 100, 70 and 20 points, the brands receive 52.6%, 36.8% and 10.5% of the market. Trust is calculated from two parameters: historical market share and the distance of the mark's shape to the reference on a scale of Hu invariant moments. With trust unchanged, organic growth does not redistribute shares.

The central thesis: the logo is an entry point and a seeding of trust. It acts at first contact, before
knowledge of the brand, through two channels — visual and verbal.


The model is considered on two cases. Mercedes and Maybach: the name Mercedes goes back
to the Latin mercēs — “reward, payment, price”; Maybach has outside German only an indirect
layer through the fragment BACH; the standalone Maybach did not hold, while under the
Mercedes mark it established itself one level lower. BYD: according to the author's hypothesis,
the distance of the mark's shape to the reference is maximal; the coincidence of the name with
words of the British Isles is accidental and did not make the brand a leader of the British market.
The value of the mark is compared with company capitalization in two separate tables.
According to Interbrand 2025 and capitalization on the same date (45 brands), the relationship is
significant: rank correlation 0.61. For the auto brands of Brand Finance 2026, the share of the
mark in capitalization ranges from 2.0% for Tesla to 116.7% for BMW; for Toyota it is 28.1%.
For each implication an observation is named that would refute it. External events (sanctions,
change of power, force majeure) are described as dated windows and are not quantified in the
model. The article is conceptual: the numbers in the model examples are conditional; the data in
Section 8 are public valuations that illustrate the relationship between the mark and value and
do not test the model.

title: Thank You, Now What? How Donors Respond to Calls to Action
affiliations: Yale School of Management, Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Reichman University and University of New Haven

detail.title: Thank You, Now What? How Donors Respond to Calls to Action

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: Conducted a field experiment with a nonprofit following their standard procedures.

detail.abstract: We study whether thank-you communications charities send to past donors should include a call to action (CTA), a direct request to give again, and show that the answer depends on whether the donor has already given in the current giving cycle. A CTA can clarify desired behavior and increase compliance, but may backfire when it asks donors to give beyond their typical cadence and violates expectations about when requests are appropriate. In a field experiment with 35,077 prior donors to a major Indian charity, we compare thank-you letters that include a CTA with otherwise identical letters without one. Response rates are low, as is typical in direct mail, with 0.69% of recipients giving. Among donors who have not yet given in the current cycle, the CTA significantly increases giving; among those who have already given, the CTA is associated with lower giving. Aggregate evaluations therefore mask heterogeneity in the CTA's effects. Because giving status within the current cycle is readily observable, charities can use it to target calls to action more effectively and improve expected fundraising revenue.

title: Competing Multi-Product Firms Using Single-Product Pricing Algorithms
affiliations: University of California, San Diego (UCSD), University College London - UCL School of Management, Boston College - Department of Marketing and Rice University

detail.abstract: Retailers increasingly price by algorithm, and recent work shows that competing singleproduct learning algorithms can reach supra-competitive prices. Most retailers, however, sell many products, and the complexity of joint pricing pushes firms toward simpler architectures: an independent algorithm for each product, or a common markup across products. Using Q-learning simulations, we show that collusive potential depends on which architecture a firm adopts. Independent single-product algorithms converge to (sub)competitive prices when products are substitutes, whereas tying products through a constant markup, or pricing them jointly, sustains supra-competitive prices. We then explain why. Once cross-product demand diversion passes a critical threshold, every unsynchronized collusive regime disappears. A constant-markup rule instead makes the problem isomorphic to single-product pricing and reinstates collusion. Descriptive evidence from Walmart, Amazon, and ZOZO shows firms using single-product algorithms in complex markets. In German gasoline duopolies, a station's matching of its rival strengthens with repricing frequency, while its two demand-independent fuels stay tightly coupled throughout, suggesting a single pricing rule spanning both fuels. For competition policy, the question is not whether firms price by algorithm, but how the algorithm spans their products.

detail.abstract: Generative AI Search places an AI-generated answer above conventional search results. This design may improve search effectiveness while changing the attention users devote to the underlying sources. These effects are particularly important for content creation platforms, where user-generated content (UGC) attracts users and user attention sustains creator participation. We examine search activity and demand for creator content in a randomized field experiment involving 100,000 users on a leading Chinese content creation platform. Treatment-group users retained access to an established Generative AI Search feature, while the platform removed access for control-group users. Access increased how often and how broadly users searched. Most additional same-day queries were classified as follow-up questions or distinct search tasks rather than revisions of earlier queries. The results reveal a scale-intensity trade-off in demand for creator content: users viewed fewer UGC previews and opened fewer UGC pages per search session, yet both totals increased over the experiment. Access also increased the number of search sessions in which users explored additional creator content after opening an initial UGC page. These findings show why engagement within individual searches can give an incomplete picture of how Generative AI Search affects overall demand for creator content.

title: Misconceptions in Mathematics Learning: A Comprehensive Literature Review of Foundations, Types, Causes, and Diagnostic Strategies

detail.title: Misconceptions in Mathematics Learning: A Comprehensive Literature Review of Foundations, Types, Causes, and Diagnostic Strategies

detail.abstract: Misconceptions in mathematics learning refer to students' understanding or ideas about mathematical concepts that are inconsistent with scientifically accepted conceptions. These misconceptions are not merely random errors but tend to be consistent, arising from students' prior knowledge, learning experiences, and the way concepts are delivered. This study aims to examine the nature, characteristics, types, causal factors, identification and diagnosis methods, as well as efforts to overcome and prevent misconceptions in mathematics learning. The study employs a literature review approach by analyzing various recent research findings related to misconceptions in mathematics education. The results indicate that misconceptions occur across various mathematical topics, including numbers and arithmetic operations, algebra, geometry, fractions, decimals and percentages, functions and equations, as well as statistics and probability, spanning from elementary school to university levels. Misconceptions are characterized by students' inaccurate understanding of concepts, misinterpretation of mathematical symbols and terms, inability to connect interrelated concepts, and gaps between conceptual understanding and application. Contributing factors include prior knowledge or preconceptions, learning experiences, difficulty understanding abstract concepts, use of mathematical language and terminology, teaching methods and strategies, instructional materials and learning resources, learning environment and teacherstudent interaction, as well as the habit of memorizing formulas without understanding concepts. Identification and diagnosis can be conducted through interviews, essay tests, three-tier tests, four-tier tests, and classroom observation. Efforts to overcome and prevent misconceptions include linking mathematical concepts to everyday experiences, using media and teaching aids, utilizing technology, and applying contextual and constructivist learning approaches. This study implies that early identification and appropriate handling of misconceptions are essential so that students can build correct and interconnected conceptual understanding.

detail.abstract: Smart learning environments combine connected classroom devices, learning analytics, and artificial intelligence to adapt content, feedback, and support. The same integration enlarges the attack surface: compromised sensors, weakly managed endpoints, manipulated telemetry, and unauthorized access can undermine both institutional security and the validity of personalization. This critical interdisciplinary review examines how machine-learning-based Internet of Things intrusion detection can be incorporated into personalized education without converting learning systems into disproportionate surveillance infrastructures. It synthesizes research on intelligent tutoring, smart learning environments, learning-analytics ethics, IoT security, intrusion-detection datasets, and AI risk governance. The literature indicates that educational effectiveness depends on timely, interpretable learner models, whereas trustworthy security depends on representative telemetry, resilience to drift and evasion, and human-governed response. These requirements overlap but are not interchangeable: a technically accurate detector may still disrupt learning, expose sensitive data, or reproduce inequities. The paper proposes SHIELD, a six-stage framework-Scope, Harden, Integrate, Evaluate, Link, and Documentthat treats educational purpose, privacy, cybersecurity, and accountability as co-designed properties. Its principal contribution is an architecture and decision model connecting learning adaptation with edge-based monitoring, data minimization, risk-tiered intervention, and auditable governance. The framework offers schools, universities, vendors, and regulators a basis for evaluating secure smart learning deployments while identifying priorities for longitudinal, adversarial, and context-sensitive validation.

detail.abstract:
A lender's decision to decline a financing request can reveal two very different problems. The borrower may lack a credible path to repayment, or the institution may lack the capacity to hold a sound transaction on acceptable terms. Confusing those situations closes off opportunities that another financing structure might support.

Recognizing the difference opens a more demanding question: can the right institutions combine their capabilities to meet the business need while preserving sound credit judgment? The answer depends on the quality of the partnership, the economics of the financing, and the decisions made throughout the loan's life. The chief lending officer (CLO) connects the institution's own capacity with capabilities available through carefully selected partners. Banks, credit unions, specialized commercial lenders, and institutional capital providers may contribute different resources to a transaction. Their participation must reflect their respective legal authority, investment mandates, and risk appetite. A partnership becomes valuable when those differences support a coherent financing structure. Its durability depends on whether the institutions can make informed decisions together when conditions change.

detail.abstract: Taking the developing Egyptian market as its focal point, the aim of this research is to contribute to the earnings management literature. Due to the limited data available for the Egyptian market, this research examines earnings management based on the entire operating performance of companies. In particular, the question of whether ineffectively performing Egyptian companies engage in upward earnings management by devising and applying income-increasing policies was investigated. For the purpose of testing for income-increasing accruals, we examine whether discretionary accruals are greater for ineffectively performing firms than for effectively performing firms. The results show that ineffectively performing Egyptian companies are characterized by positive and considerably greater discretionary accruals when comparatively examined against effectively performing companies. A reasonable interpretation of these results is that ineffectively performing companies engage in earnings management practices, with the most likely mechanism being an opportunistic increase in their reported earnings. Overall, the findings of this study show that operating performance is a critical determinant of earnings management. In terms of the implications of these findings, it is necessary for officials within the Egyptian government to enhance the country's corporate governance processes, especially in view of the limitations surrounding law enforcement and investor safeguards.

detail.abstract: The paper examines opportunities for deeper economic integration between the EU and the Western Balkans and assesses their potential economic impact. It documents key non-tariff barriers to Western Balkan–EU industrial goods trade—covering regulatory, customs, and border-logistics frictions—amounting to around 8–14 percent ad valorem equivalent. Reducing these barriers, alongside deeper agri-food and services integration, could generate substantial gains, allowing the Western Balkans to capture roughly one-quarter to one-half of the economic benefits of full EU membership while supporting EU objectives related to nearshoring, supply-chain resilience, regional integration, and connectivity.

detail.abstract: Domestic markets can be far from fully integrated within a country: Canada's interprovincial trade is half the size of its international trade. We estimate internal trade costs using bilateral flows across hundreds of products and sectors and decompose them into geographic and non-geographic components. Embedding these estimates in a multi-region, multi-sector general equilibrium model with input–output linkages and interprovincial migration, we find that removing all non-distance barriers raises real GDP by 6.8 percent in our baseline scenario, with the largest gains accruing to smaller provinces. We also identify services as the sectors generating the largest liberalization gains. Further, sequential provincial liberalization can generate a virtuous cycle, where a province's liberalization increases the gains from (and incentives for) subsequent liberalization for most other following provinces. Finally, we show that the potential gains from domestic market integration can offset the GDP losses from increases in external trade costs.

detail.abstract:
This preprint presents a critical empirical and methodological evaluation of the widely repeated claim that public ignorance has grown in the age of the information explosion. Drawing on longitudinal survey data across nine epistemic domains (from scientific, political, and financial literacy to misinformation prevalence, health literacy, and news infrastructure) the paper breaks down the monolithic concept of ignorance into testable components. 
The claim that public ignorance has grown appears repeatedly in public discourse and even in parts of the academic literature, from Hofstadter to Haidt, yet it has rarely been tested against independent, longitudinal empirical evidence. This paper breaks the claim down into measurable cases and tests each one against real survey data. The method rests on two pillars. 
First, it treats ignorance as a multi-component vector rather than a one-dimensional scalar: the absence of knowledge, false belief, miscalibration, deliberate doubt production, and functional mismatch must be measured separately. 
Second, it applies a three-condition decision rule fixed before the data were examined, to prevent selective reading of the evidence. On this basis, nine epistemic domains, from scientific and political knowledge to financial literacy, health literacy, reading, and the quality of local news infrastructure, were tested against data from the NSF, Pew, FINRA, OECD, and Eurobarometer. The result is not one-sided. Of twelve cases examined, only two show a defensible decline, one shows a defensible rise, and nearly half are methodologically undecidable. 
This heterogeneity itself supports the paper's three central findings: the original claim, before it is broken down, is an incomplete statement rather than a false one; the empirical evidence does not support a single uniform trend; and the shared error of both proponents and critics of the claim is generalising a finding from one level of analysis to another. The paper's thesis is not that the claim is false, but that it cannot be judged at all before it is broken down, and what that breakdown yields, in place of a simple answer, is a map.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the effect of alternative digital lending—defined as digital credit provision by non‑bank financial intermediaries (NBFIs)—on bank and systemic risk taking and competition. The paper focuses on Sociedades Financieras Populares (SOFIPOs) which constitute a regulated and well‑documented NBFI segment allowing an empirical assessment of the relationship between digital non-bank lending expansion and bank outcomes. Using a quarterly sample of 53 Mexican banks and 8 of these non-banks for the period 2018Q1–2024Q4, we document that growth in alternative digital lending is associated with lower individual bank risk-taking and stronger competitive pressures, with the latter effect being stronger for small banks. Reflecting the moderate size of digital lenders in Mexico and the compositional reallocation between bank and non‑bank credit, overall systemic risk appears broadly unaltered by the entry of the new players.

detail.abstract: We study online resource allocation with known time-varying arrivals. Under an aggregate general position gap (GPG) and a uniform persistent-support condition, we construct slack-preserving period-wise resource targets. The targets retain the aggregate optimal price and transfer the GPG uniformly across periods, a property not guaranteed by proportional disaggregation of common optimality alone. The resulting primal-dual policy solves one LP before the horizon and achieves O(1) expected regret relative to the hindsight optimum, without requiring a unique aggregate primal optimum.

detail.abstract: India's data centre sector is undergoing rapid expansion, with installed IT load capacity reaching 1.4 GW by mid-2025 and projected to double within two years. This growth is materially constrained by electricity availability, grid carbon intensity, and water stress-pressures that remain largely ungoverned. India's nascent carbon market, the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), formally notified in June 2023 and moving toward compliance trading in 2026, currently covers nine energyintensive industrial sectors; data centres are explicitly identified for a second tranche. Meanwhile, state governments compete aggressively for data centre investment through land subsidies, electricity duty waivers, power tariff concessions, and fast-track approvals-instruments that suppress the energy price signal the carbon market depends upon. This paper analyses the structural misalignment between the national carbon market and state-level digital industrial policies, examining whether a carbon pricing mechanism can effectively govern data centre growth when subnational governments actively undercut its price signal. Using multi-level governance theory as an analytical framework and applying institutional analysis to policy documents, the paper identifies four dimensions of misalignment: price signal suppression, absent water governance, weak renewable energy conditionality, and interstate coordination failure. It argues that without integrating data centres into the CCTS compliance mechanism, linking state incentives to minimum sustainability standards, and establishing a central-state coordination compact, India risks deepening electricity-system stress, water pressure, and fossil-fuel lock-in in its digital infrastructure sector. The paper proposes a set of policy alignment mechanisms oriented toward SDG 7 (affordable and clean energy) and SDG 11 (sustainable cities and communities).

detail.abstract: Kenya's Supreme Court has decided four presidential election petitions since 2013, and each time it has spoken as though deciding for the first time. This paper reads the four decisions Odinga v IEBC (2013), Odinga v IEBC (2017), Mwau v IEBC (2017), and Odinga v Ruto (2022) as one continuous text, and asks whether the Court's jurisprudence has developed or merely repeated itself in louder language. It finds neither steady progress nor honest retreat, but a pattern of convenient doubt: standards of proof, evidentiary burdens, and the meaning of verification shift according to whether the Court wishes to disturb an outcome, not according to any consistently stated principle of interpretation. The 2017 annulment, celebrated as Africa's boldest judicial moment, sits uneasily beside 2013 and 2022, both of which return to a jurisprudence of deference dressed in the vocabulary of process. Drawing on commentaries, this paper argues that Kenya's electionpetition jurisprudence is not incoherent by accident but structured by an unacknowledged doctrine: the Court protects finality first and constitutionalism second, and calls the arrangement law. The paper proposes evidentiary reform, not doctrinal recalibration, as the more durable corrective.

detail.abstract: This paper examines debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing in Brazil as a test of whether a super-priority transplant delivers its predicted gains. Lei 14.112/2020 imported the logic of §364 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code into the Lei de Recuperação de Empresas e Falência (arts. 69-A to 69-F and art. 84, I-B), raising de jure protection of the DIP financier from near-absence to near-completeness. We measure that step using an index of statutory protection across ten dimensions, with a maximum of 11 points, rising from 1 of 11 before the reform to 10.5 of 11 after it. The half point withheld is itself a finding, and it records a structural incompatibility rather than a drafting choice. The DIP lender may take fiduciary security over unencumbered assets, and in practice does, but art. 69-C, §2º places assets already under fiduciary title beyond the reach of the new priming power, because title sits with the creditor and leaves nothing of the debtor’s to subordinate. Since fiduciary positions dominate Brazilian secured credit, the priming mechanism arrived with little to prime. We then benchmark this statutory framework against a hand-collected census of 35 documented distressed-financing operations, 22 of which are confirmed Brazilian-law DIP facilities. The de facto findings are three. Penetration is thin even in a size-matched comparison, at roughly 3% of large-company reorganizations, compared with roughly 62% in the U.S. benchmark. Observed pricing is bimodal, either insider money priced below any market reference or arm's-length money priced at multiples of the U.S. mean spread, with almost nothing in between. And the market is opaque by intention and design, with lender identity, price, and collateral routinely outside the public record. We attribute this profile to three frictions between the statute and the market, namely judicial discretion in recognizing extraconcursal priority, variability in the enforcement of fiduciary collateral, and concentration among distressed-credit lenders, operating on an embryonic structured-credit market and an insolvency culture whose filing population is dominated by micro and small firms. We are explicit that the reform created a market where almost none existed, that the de facto layer is descriptive rather than causal, and that the Brazilian disclosure environment does not permit observation of the full population of DIP instruments or of their financial terms. Our design treats that opacity as a documented feature of the data rather than an assumption to be waved away.

detail.abstract: Digital payment channels, cloud services and third-party platforms are becoming the tools of the small to midsize businesses (SMBs), but companies of this scale often aren't equipped with the tools for specialised business analytics and security employees that larger companies may possess. This gives rise to an imbalance of vulnerability that puts SMEs at a greater risk of financial fraud attacks and is increasingly automated, sometimes supported by generative artificial intelligence. This paper suggests an AI-enabled cyberfinancial resilience framework that brings together the three components: machine learning for fraud detection, fusion of cyber threat intelligence (CTI) and risk-based decision making and defines the appropriate single operational architecture for SME constraints. It is structured in three layers, each of which interacts with the other: data and sensing, AI level 2 analytics core, risk based decisions and responses, where there is also a module of explainability and a process of continuous feedback for retraining the model. The architecture is derived by carrying out a structured literature review of the current fraud detection (FD) and cyber threat intelligence (CTI) + enterprise risk management (ERM) bodies of literature, and an illustrative simulated scenario is employed to illustrate how the FD+ERM/CTI framework's fused-scoring approach can enhance detection of fraud by minimizing false-positive rates, and augment detection consistency relative to a rule-based and standalone machine-learning baselines. Governance, explainability, data quality and cost issues that arise and affect whether such a framework is feasible in resource-constrained organisations are discussed. The paper proposes a modular, adoption-friendly reference architecture that bridges three literatures which are not commonly seen together in SME-specific studies and highlights practical, ethical, and regulatory constraints to be overcome for large-scale deployment.

detail.abstract:
In January 2021, retail broker-dealer Robinhood abruptly restricted trading in GameStop and other “meme” stocks, sparking public outrage and political scrutiny. While conspiracy theories spread quickly, a more mundane structural explanation soon emerged: Robinhood’s restrictions were driven by its contractual obligation to meet collateral requirements imposed by the National Securities Clearing Corporation (NSCC), the principal clearinghouse for broker-to-broker transactions in U.S. equity and certain debt securities.

This Article uses the Robinhood episode to examine three often overlooked dimensions of the obscure yet crucial post-trade infrastructure underpinning modern markets. First, securities transactions do not settle instantly: A period of latency separates trade execution from final settlement, creating time for multilateral netting while prolonging counterparty exposure. Second, drawing on Ronald Coase’s theory of the firm, the analysis explains the economic logic behind the rise and persistence of specialized post-trade intermediaries such as NSCC. Third, it examines how blockchain, tokenization, and related financial technologies challenge—but may also be incorporated into—the existing intermediated architecture for clearing and settlement.

Far from being relics of an obsolete market structure, post-trade infrastructures, clearinghouses in particular, are institutional solutions to the transaction costs of multilateral securities markets. Their persistence reflects economic logic, not institutional atrophy. Technological innovation may nevertheless alter the relative costs of existing institutional arrangements and create new ways to perform post-trade functions. Rather than pursuing wholesale disruption, regulators should therefore adopt an incremental and experimental approach to modernization—one that fosters innovation, promotes efficiency, preserves market stability, and generates the institutional knowledge necessary for the post-trade system’s future evolution.

detail.abstract: Millions of Americans live in "pharmacy deserts"-communities with no meaningful access to a retail pharmacy-and this burden falls disproportionately on low-income, minority, rural, and medically underserved populations. At the same time, the national pharmaceutical supply chain continues to experience record numbers of drug shortages, driven by limited upstream visibility and reactive, rather than predictive, planning. This paper proposes PharmaBridge AI, a conceptual framework that applies artificial intelligence across four integrated layers of the medicine supply chain-demand forecasting and shortage prediction, intelligent distribution and last-mile delivery, AI-assisted care delivery to physicians, pharmacists, and patients, and an equity-and-access layer that explicitly targets pharmacy deserts-to shorten the distance between manufactured medicine and the patient who needs it. The framework is grounded in the existing, real-world evidence base: geospatial studies documenting the scale and demographic pattern of US pharmacy deserts, published industry analyses of AI-based demand-sensing for drug-shortage prediction, and operational drone and autonomous-vehicle pilots already used to deliver medicine to rural US clinics. The paper discusses how such a system would need to be evaluated, the barriers to responsible deployment-including data governance, workforce impact, algorithmic bias, and the risk of automating existing inequities-and concludes that AI, deliberately designed around equity metrics rather than efficiency alone, offers a credible path toward more reliable medicine access for underserved American communities.

detail.abstract: Entrepreneurs and managers often need to evaluate strategic choices, such as redesigning an incentive plan or entering an unfamiliar market, before committing scarce resources. Existing offline search tools, including mental models, analogical reasoning, model building, and simulation, allow managers to weigh alternatives without acting, but each is limited by what a single decision maker can specify, recall, or imagine. We argue that advances in generative AI, combined with the growing availability of firm-specific digital trace data, are transforming this tradeoff. We introduce the organizational digital twin (ODT), an infrastructure combining firm-specific data, AI-based behavioral simulation models, and governance rules which facilitates a new form of offline search that we call learning-by-twinning: search conducted by observing how a strategic choice unfolds within a digital replica of the firm. We identify three mechanisms through which learning-by-twinning creates value, namely expanded search, safer experimentation, and richer system-level feedback as well as specify certain conditions under which these benefits may attenuate.

detail.abstract: This review of John Lemos's Free Will's Value: Criminal Justice, Pride, and Love presents two central contributions of the book: an indeterministic weightings model of libertarian free will, developed from Robert Kane's event-causal libertarianism, and a pragmatic argument that we ought to live as if we possess such free will because of its value for criminal justice, pride, and love. The review argues that Lemos's model plausibly avoids the phenomenological and irrationality objections to Kane's model of dual efforts of will. It also raises questions about how Lemos weighs the value of human dignity against the value of fairness in criminal law, and about the dependence of libertarian free-willed love on the beloved's recognition of such love.

detail.abstract: Menstrual leave has moved in a single year from a scattered welfare practice into a contested constitutional question in India. Karnataka's 2025 policy, upheld by its High Court in April 2026, sits alongside a Supreme Court that in March 2026 declined to mandate a national scheme, warning explicitly that a compulsory, gender-specific entitlement could make employers reluctant to hire women at all. This article examines whether menstrual leave, as an instrument of human resource policy, advances gender justice or instead functions as a hidden barrier to women's employment. Drawing on statistical-discrimination theory, comparative evidence from Japan, Spain, Indonesia, Taiwan, South Korea and Zambia, and the closely analogous domestic experience of the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, the article argues that the employment effect of menstrual leave is not fixed by the fact of mandation but by its design. A rigid, women-only, medically-certified entitlement recreates the very cost signal that depressed female hiring after the 2017 maternity amendment; a flexible, gender-neutral, self-certified entitlement embedded in a wider wellness architecture need not. The article closes with a set of design and implementation recommendations for HR practitioners operating in a fragmented, rapidly evolving regulatory environment.

detail.abstract: Drawing on dynamic capability theory, this study examines how green intellectual capital contributes to environmental performance in Chinese manufacturing firms. Using two-wave survey data from 417 managers, this study combines partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), necessary condition analysis (NCA), and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to capture net effects, necessary conditions, and configurational pathways of environmental performance. These three methods offer complementary evidence on symmetric effects, necessity logic, and configurational sufficiency. The PLS-SEM results indicate that green absorptive capacity mediates the relationship between green intellectual capital and environmental performance. AI-infused knowledge strengthens the conversion of green intellectual capital into green absorptive capacity by improving green knowledge processing. The NCA results suggest that green human capital, green structural capital, and green relational capital must reach minimum levels for firms to attain high environmental performance. The fsQCA results further identify multiple functionally equivalent configurations leading to high environmental performance. Beyond green knowledge resources, green absorptive capacity, AI-infused knowledge, and the configurational alignment are critical to achieving superior environmental performance. These findings advance the green intellectual capital literature by clarifying the complementary roles of these factors in driving environmental performance.

TRACE: The UCC Instantiated under "Unknown Goal + Divergent Pressure" . . . . . 5 4. PDCA: The UCC Instantiated under "Known Goal + Convergent Pressure" . . . . . . 10 cognitive cycle

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a Unified Cognitive Cycle (UCC) framework and argues that all cognitive activity—from scientific research to engineering improvement—shares one deep structure: candi date → testing → selection. On this structure, UCC possesses two degrees of freedom: the goal state (known or unknown) and the pressure direction (convergent or divergent). Two widely used methodologies are shown to be instances of UCC under two extreme configurations: • TRACE (Traverse–Refute–Anomaly–Converge–Establish) is the unfolding of UCC under “unknown goal + divergent pressure,” that is, the discovery cycle—its function is to com press the space of errors and to make unconsidered possibilities visible. • PDCA (Plan–Do–Check–Act) is the unfolding of UCC under “known goal + convergent pressure,” that is, the improvement cycle—its function is to optimize a process within a given goal. The central claim of this paper is that TRACE is more fundamental than PDCA. All im provement presupposes that the goal has already been determined, whereas “goal determination” itself must first pass through a discovery. Therefore PDCA is a degenerate special case of TRACE under the constraint of a “known goal”—once discovery is complete and the goal is locked, UCC converges into PDCA. This paper provides a unified operator mapping from TRACE and PDCA to UCC, argues that the two are structurally isomorphic while semantically heterogeneous, and sets out three criteria for meta-method falsifiability (cross-case reproducibility, anomaly identification rate, and the effectiveness of the division of labor over errors). On the evidential level, this paper does two things. First, it supports the core claim with cross domain internal cases from the Spectral Abyss (graph theory) and the stock market (finance); second, it conducts a structural test (§7) using a set of documented historical cases—eleven in total: four main cases (Semmelweis and puerperal fever, penicillin, the Michelson–Morley null result, and sildenafil), five contemporary control cases (John Snow, Dubos, Le Verrier, minoxidil, and thalidomide), and two repeatedly told “suppressed” negative cases (McClintock and Wegener). This test is not empirical; rather, it examines whether the five operators of UCC can be identified in real history and whether the points of failure can be precisely located. The payoff of this test is three theoretical revisions: the C (converge) stage requires a “patch self check” (including a free-parameter criterion) and a “tension self-check”; the E (establish) stage must satisfy four conditions—“mechanistic explainability / social acceptability / adjacent capabilities and institutions / action decouplability”; and the test additionally reveals an institutional obstacle: monitoring systems record only harm (ADR) and not benefit (BDR). These revisions have been written back into §3.4. At the same time, the test also downgrades the support strength of several cases (sildenafil cannot support “the original goal was wrong”; the “suppressed” narratives of McClintock and Wegener are narrowed after verification)—this paper reports these weakenings honestly, and not only the strengthenings. Honest declaration. This paper is a formal model of cognitive structure, not an empirical mathematical paper. Its output depends on the honest execution of its users rather than on validation by experimental data. The model itself is not exempt from its own testing criteria (see §8). The historical cases in §7 are structural illustrations and do not constitute evidence for the validity of the theory.

detail.abstract: The first Miracle on the Han River was built on a promise: that labor, like scaffolding, could be temporary. In South Korea's super-aged society, that promise has become the problem, generating what this study terms integration waste: the structural loss of host-country integration gains under temporal visa rotation. Drawing on five years of longitudinal qualitative fieldwork tracking Filipino migrants across key visa categories, this study evaluates how the Employment Permit System's dual-track framework produces integration waste through civic stratification under compressed modernity. Comparing fixed E-9 rotation against the E-7-4 skilled worker transition and state-sanctioned F-6 family integration, the analysis demonstrates that integration waste is a structural byproduct produced directly by visa category design. The study yields four institutional implications for demographic sustainability and argues that localized retention pathways represent a critical strategic transition for regional stabilization.

detail.abstract: Published studies name several series that should add to the yield curve as a predictor of recessions. I asked whether adding one of them to a probit on the spread between the 10-year Treasury yield and the 3-month bill rate would have improved its 12-month recession probabilities in real time. Six series were tested: the 5-year, 1-year and 10-year Treasury yields and the yield on Moody's highest-rated (Aaa) corporate bonds, each less the federal funds rate (the overnight rate the Federal Reserve targets), the S&P 500 and building permits. The protocol, written and dated before I scored any forecast, starts with a check on the comparison itself, a simulation in which the added series helps by a known amount. None of the six series passed. If a series lowered the curve's expected log score, a penalty for inaccurate probability forecasts, by 20 percent, the comparison called it better in 15 percent of simulated histories at most, and its intervals missed the true difference more often than the protocol allowed. There have been about eight recessions since the mid-1960s, and three since real-time permits data begin, too few for this procedure to tell a gain of a fifth from none. I report the historical scores, and the forecasts made during the 2022–24 false alarm, as description only.

detail.abstract: A member of a community health pool pays every year and never claims. By insurance logic, she should be the first to leave. She often stays, and dual benefit is what holds her: her own return is worth more as the collective's output grows, a coupling measured by the cross-partial δ ≡ ∂²W/∂G∂M between collective output G and personal benefit M, zero when the benefit separates. The coupling changes who exits: under separability, the non-claimant leaves first; where the collective channels are legible and clear, the premium, she renews, so lemons selection switches off. Two results carry the paper. A pool retains a stable, positive membership if and only if δ exceeds a critical value δ*, at which the participation dynamics fold in a saddle-node bifurcation; where the collective channels are closed to the member, the non-claimants leave first, an unraveling like Akerlof's. And where δ > 0, what the collective adds differs across members by δ·G·ΔM, so no single cash transfer fits all, and the best one is out by half that gap: the coupling cannot be bought out. The testable content is about staying, not joining. Indian panel data show illness does not predict who joins, but delivered benefit does predict who stays, and a five-year Nepal renewal panel shows the claimant–non-claimant gap widening with tenure on the log-odds scale, the sign the coupling predicts.

detail.abstract: This working paper analyses the fiscal and macroeconomic consequences of Zambia's five-month fuel tax suspension, implemented in response to an unprecedented external oil price shock triggered by the near-complete closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the escalation of conflict on 28 February 2026 in the Middle East. The shock drove international petroleum product prices sharply upward: petrol prices rose by 62.84 percent (from USD 70.32 to USD 114.51 per barrel), diesel by 91.89 percent (from USD 84.74 to USD 162.61 per barrel), and kerosene/Jet A-1 by 102.41 percent (from USD 83.95 to USD 169.92 per barrel)-as confirmed by the Energy Regulation Board (ERB) in its April 2026 price review. Over the same period, the Zambian Kwacha depreciated from K19.18 to K19.30 per US dollar, further amplifying the domestic cost impact. These combined pressures significantly increased Zambia's fuel import bill and placed acute pressure on household welfare, transport costs, and industrial production. In response, the Government of the Republic of Zambia announced the zero rating of Value Added Tax (VAT) and the suspension of Excise Duty on petrol and diesel imports for a period of five months, from 1st April to 31st August 2026. Using a combination of fiscal modelling, price pass-through analysis, and social sector sensitivity mapping, this paper estimates that the zero rating of VAT and suspension of Excise Duty will cost the fiscus approximately ZMW 2.35 billion to ZMW 2.65 billion in foregone revenue over the fivemonth window (April to August 2026), equivalent to roughly 1.1 to 1.3 percent of the 2026 national domestic revenue target of K206.5 billion. Marez holds a Masters in Economics from the University of Lusaka, and is currently pursing a Bachelor of Arts in Accounting from the University of Leads 2 Moses Mukambo Jr-Moses Serves as the Director Finance & Administration at the Zambia Youth Delivery Forum. As a certified Investment advisor, prior to this role, Moses worked in investment Banking space and joined the public sector where he was instrumental in budgeting and RMNC+ health reform. At the post-shock price level of USD 120 per barrel, the annual import bill rises to an estimated USD 1.18 billion, a USD 445 million increase that directly erodes the current account and tightens the fiscal space within which the tax suspension must be managed. The paper further assesses the vulnerability of youth and social sector spending, including skills development, health, education, and social cash transfers to compensatory expenditure adjustments that may be required to close the fiscal gap. We identify four fiscal scenarios based on the duration of the geopolitical conflict and the government's policy choices, and propose revenue-neutral and revenue-positive alternatives to protect social spending while maintaining fiscal discipline. The findings underscore the need for a pre-committed social sector protection framework and alternative revenue mobilisation measures, including a windfall levy on fuel retailers and targeted borrowing, to prevent the welfare gains of the tax suspension from being offset by cuts to youth and social programmes.

detail.abstract: Human resources (HR) are strategic assets that determine the success of an organization in achieving its goals. This chapter discusses the concept and scope of training, development, and Human Resource Development (HRD) strategies. The discussion begins with the definition of HR management according to experts, its elements, functions, roles, and goals. Furthermore, the concept of HRD and its theoretical foundations are explained, namely organizational development, economic theory, and human capital theory. This chapter also describes the meaning of training and development, the differences between the two, and their goals and benefits for employees, organizations, and employment relationships. Training is oriented towards improving the ability for current jobs, while development is oriented towards readiness to face future needs. The scope of HRD includes HR planning, education and training, career development, work experience, counseling, and organizational development. The role of HRD is viewed from the strategic, operational, and transformational sides, with functions that include planning to employee termination. HRD strategies are realized through work programs such as recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management, compensation, employee engagement, succession planning, and HR analytics. These programs need to be aligned with the organization's vision, mission, and strategy. In the modern era, HRD faces challenges in the form of digital transformation, the use of artificial intelligence, digital competency gaps, data security risks, and resistance to change. Therefore, HRD is required to be proactive and adaptive so that organizations have competent and competitive human resources.

detail.abstract: At the turn of the twentieth century, the movement against what was then commonly described as the "white slave trade" became an important part of British social reform, public morality, and international cooperation. The term "white slave trade" referred primarily to the alleged movement of women and girls across national borders for prostitution and other forms of sexual exploitation. Although the language used by contemporaries was often sensational and carried racial and moral assumptions, the campaign contributed to the development of organised efforts against the exploitation of women and to the emergence of international cooperation on trafficking. This article examines the relationship between gender, migration and British antitrafficking efforts between the late nineteenth century and approximately 1909, with particular attention to the National Vigilance Association (NVA). It explores how voluntary organisations, reformers, government officials and international institutions responded to the perceived movement of women across borders. The article argues that British anti-trafficking activism was shaped by two closely connected concerns: the protection of vulnerable women and the regulation of female sexuality and migration. The National Vigilance Association played a significant role by organising campaigns, gathering information, cooperating with authorities and helping to establish the International Bureau for the Suppression of the White Slave Traffic in 1899. Britain subsequently participated in international arrangements, including the 1904 International Agreement for the Suppression of the "White Slave Traffic." At the same time, these efforts were not free from contradictions. Campaigners frequently presented British women as innocent victims and foreign men as threats, while giving less attention to the economic and social circumstances that influenced women's migration. The article therefore considers anti-trafficking activism as both a humanitarian project and a form of social regulation. By examining the gendered and migratory dimensions of the campaign, it contributes to a better understanding of the historical foundations of modern anti-trafficking policies.

detail.abstract: The increasing heterogeneity of services supported by fifth-generation (5G) and emerging sixth-generation (6G) telecommunications networks creates substantial challenges for dynamic resource management. Network slicing enables multiple virtual networks to share common physical infrastructure while maintaining differentiated service requirements, but conventional static and reactive allocation strategies may struggle with rapidly changing traffic, competing resource demands, and stringent Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. This paper presents a literaturebased synthesis of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches to dynamic network slicing and resource management, with particular methodological and empirical attention given to the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MA-DDPG) framework developed by Onaji et al. (2025). The primary study models network slices as cooperative agents using Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) and evaluates the approach in a custom Discrete-Event Network Slice Simulator (DENS-Sim). Its reported results indicate that MA-DDPG can improve resource utilization efficiency while reducing service-level agreement violations and over-provisioning relative to the study's centralized DQN and Greedy benchmarks. The broader literature extends this direction toward AI-enabled resource allocation, radio scheduling, digital twins, explainable AI, mobility management, energy efficiency, and 5Gto-6G transition frameworks. Building on these findings, this paper proposes a conceptual synthesis in which dynamic slicing combines multi-agent learning, predictive resource allocation, explainability, resilience, and energy-aware orchestration. The framework is literature-grounded and is not presented as independently empirically validated.

detail.abstract: Research funding rules affect both which projects receive support and how researchers disclose information. We study a competitive information design model in which researchers, whose applications differ in public track records and distributions of project quality, choose disclosure schemes before observing private evidence about their projects, and a research funding agency commits ex ante to a mechanism for allocating at most k awards based on posterior assessments. With one researcher, we show that an appropriately chosen threshold on posterior expected project value induces a simple disclosure equilibrium and attains the first-best result. With multiple researchers, ranking projects by posterior value may fail to admit an equilibrium. We propose a threshold-plus-lottery mechanism that combines individual reservation thresholds reflecting funding costs with a common competitive threshold reflecting limited capacity. A uniform lottery allocates awards when the qualified researchers outnumber the funding slots. This mechanism admits an equilibrium where each researcher uses a cutoff equal to the maximum of a cost floor and a competition-induced cutoff. It guarantees at least (1/2) [1 - (e⁻ᵏ · kᵏ) / k!] of the first-best expected utility. A sharper guarantee holds for project value distributions with monotone hazard rates in a setting with zero funding cost and no overqualified researchers. Our results provide practical guidance for research-funding design under strategic disclosure and capacity constraints.

detail.abstract: The success of training and human resource development (HR) is highly dependent on the accuracy of the organization in identifying the actual needs. This chapter discusses three main concepts that are the basis for analyzing these needs, namely strategic alignment, performance gap, and competency gap. Strategic alignment is understood as the alignment of Human Resource Development (HRD) strategies, policies, and practices with the organization's vision, mission, and goals, both vertically and horizontally. Its application provides benefits for performance and productivity, but faces challenges in the form of environmental changes, digital transformation, and digital skills gaps. Performance gap is the difference between expected performance and actual performance, the causes of which need to be analyzed before determining an intervention. Competency gap is the difference between the competencies required by a position and the competencies that employees have, and can be overcome through tailored training, succession planning, and communication and collaboration. The three concepts meet in Training Needs Analysis (TNA) which includes organizational, occupational, and individual level analysis, prioritization, planning, and program evaluation. The interconnectedness of the three forms a continuous cycle that ensures training is on target, aligned with organizational strategy, and has an impact on improving organizational performance and competitiveness.

detail.abstract: Government loan guarantees support SMEs worldwide, but program evaluations usually treat them as bank-firm credit products and ignore the supply chain context. A strategic supplier can adjust the wholesale price in response to a guarantee, and demand uncertainty adds operational risk absent from standard guarantee models. We incorporate a government guarantee in a newsvendor supply chain with a Stackelberg supplier, a capital-constrained retailer, and a competitive bank. Where pass-through is positive, a stronger guarantee raises the wholesale price, and the supplier captures part of the relief, while the retailer can be worse off than under no guarantee. Default risk can rise when lower borrowing costs induce higher borrowing amounts. At high coverage, loan spreads can approach zero even as default risk remains positive, making spreads a poor proxy for borrower or government risk. Furthermore, the government guarantee alone need not materially raise supply-chain efficiency. In the numerical analysis, higher demand variability and coverage increase default risk and expected government payments. Retailers with low working capital generate more incremental credit and larger expected government payments. Partial trade credit can raise efficiency and reduce government exposure simultaneously. A uniform coverage ratio has heterogeneous fiscal consequences. These results suggest that differentiated coverage by borrower wealth and demand risk is desirable.

detail.abstract:
In September 2026, an independent investigation found that the Los Angeles Clippers basketball team spent years secretly routing millions of dollars to superstar player Kawhi Leonard through companies doing business with the team. Every NBA franchise operates under a salary cap, which is a limit on player pay that is agreed to through the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) with the league and the players’ union. This Article argues that the Clippers’ scheme is not an isolated failure, but a preview of what may happen given private equity ownership now present in the major professional sports leagues.

 

Salary caps are a restraint on trade that benefits owners, but it survives antitrust scrutiny because it satisfies the non-statutory labor exemption, a judge-made rule that shields agreements in the CBA from ordinary antitrust law. To qualify, a restraint must affect only the bargaining parties, concern a mandatory subject like wages, and, most importantly here, be the product of a real, good faith negotiation that the parties follow once signed. Circumventing the salary cap puts this third prong at risk.

 

The Clippers investigation is a case study for that risk. Private equity funds now hold stakes in a majority of NBA franchises. They have little say over day to day decisions, but every incentive to see their team win, since a championship can add billions to a franchise’s value before the fund exits. That incentive, combined with these funds’ large and often undisclosed business holdings, creates new and largely invisible ways to pay a star player more than the cap allows. If such arrangements become common, the League’s good faith compliance breaks down, and with it, the legal shield protecting the salary cap itself.

 

This Article proposes concrete reforms for the League’s next collective bargaining agreement: a joint oversight board to monitor player endorsements and owner investments, clearer rules distinguishing legitimate business dealings from hidden pay, and penalties tied directly to the amount diverted. The stakes reach beyond one team or only the NBA. Every major North American sports league now operates under a salary cap or comparable constraint and has also permitted private equity investment within the past several years. If circumvention of the salary cap becomes widespread and effectively unchecked, it threatens not only the salary cap’s effectiveness, but also the antitrust shield enjoyed by the leagues.  Without reform, the good faith foundation of the non-statutory labor exemption will remain exposed, not just for the NBA, but for every league facing the same pressures.

detail.abstract: Mechanical face seal maintenance requires decisions about when condition information justifies replacement and which assets should receive limited maintenance resources. This study asks how seal condition and operating history can improve prioritisation compared with fixed replacement intervals and static criticality ranking. Because the preceding manuscript's industrial records were unavailable for verification, a reproducible computational experiment was executed for an explicitly simulated population of 60 liquid lubricated mechanical face seals in non potable water service centrifugal pumps. A gamma degradation model represented monotonic loss of condition; temperature, pressure, start stop cycles and persistent installation heterogeneity determined operating hour degradation rates. Four policies were compared across 156 weekly decisions and 100 independent replications: fixed interval replacement, static consequence ranking, a simple condition threshold and a one week probability weighted economic priority. All policies shared scheduled maintenance capacity, precautionary stop rules, replacement effects and cost accounting. Outcomes included failure events, unplanned stops, maintenance workload, downtime and assumed monetary costs. In the base scenario, mean simulated failures were 29.82, 32.19, 6.49 and 34.84, respectively. Mean costs were USD 2.005, 1.792, 1.056 and 1.722 million in assumed scenario currency. Dynamic ranking reduced cost relative to the two age eligible policies but performed substantially worse than the condition threshold; its lower planned replacement workload was offset by precautionary stops and failures. Sensitivity experiments showed dependence on capacity, forecast assumptions, condition noise and failure consequences. These findings demonstrate a decision trade off within the specified model, rather than industrial predictive accuracy or validated shutdown reduction. A short horizon economic rule can defer intervention excessively, whereas a transparent threshold can exploit informative condition measurements effectively. Field implementation requires seal specific calibration, independent evaluation and author reviewed engineering safeguards.
